risks.note: The Company's financial asset is mainly investment in listed security, so any material volatility in the capital market may impact the market value of the investment. Income from investments (dividend on equity shares and mutual funds and interest on bank fixed deposits) is disclosed in the BRSR as a large share of turnover, and the year's step-up in other income and profit was attributed to a higher dividend declaration by UPL Limited of 300% versus 50% in the previous year - making earnings dependent on one investee's payout decision.

As there are only trading activities in the Company, it may not be able to mobilize adequate funds, if any, in time. Management's stated mitigant is that the Company has good investment in quoted shares, so raising additional funds, if any, will not be difficult.

risks.risk: Trading business / counterparty and contract-performance risk
risks.note: Deals in agro commodities, metals and chemicals are done through sale and purchase contracts at pre-determined rates and quantities with the help of market intermediaries; there can be risks of unfulfillment of contractual terms - non-delivery, late or short delivery, quality issues on the supply side and non-payment from the customer side. The Company also transacts on the MCX Commodity platform through an intermediary registered with MCX/SEBI, doing deals only when spot and future rates differ.

The Company is engaged only in trading and operates in a single segment; exports are reported as 'Not Applicable-0%' of turnover, employees work for the Company on deputation and it has no workers, so the business depends on group resources and on a narrow activity base with no diversification cushion.

Any change in Government / Regulators Policy / Rules / Regulations will require fresh compliances; the stated mitigant is that the group has a very strong and dedicated team of professionals to study regulatory changes and fresh requirements.

Trading activities may be subject to the risk of lower profit or loss on account of volatility in foreign currency exchange; management states it structures trading transactions so that such volatility risk is minimal, or may take adequate forward cover.

The Company is subject to risks associated with IT and cybersecurity relating to cybercrime and theft of sensitive information; mitigants cited are group IT infrastructure and security systems with robust firewalls and disaster recovery mechanisms, perpetual event monitoring, access controls and employee education on safe practices.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Continue to look at new opportunities of trading, remaining a single-segment trading company (agro commodities, metals, chemicals)
- Run trading directly in the market through sale and purchase contracts at pre-determined rates and quantities with the help of market intermediaries, and on the MCX Commodity platform only when there is a difference between spot rates and future rates on available MCX future contracts
- Hold investments in listed securities and mutual funds as a second income stream - dividend on equity shares and mutual funds and interest on bank fixed deposits
- Structure trading transactions so that there are minimal risks of foreign-currency volatility, or take adequate forward cover for foreign exchange fluctuations
- Maintain internal financial controls commensurate with the size, scale and complexity of operations, with the internal audit function outsourced and findings tracked to closure by the Audit Committee
- Dividend: the Directors' dividend recommendation is stated to be in line with the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy, which is published on the Company's website under the Investors section; the dividend for FY2025-26 is put to members as an ordinary resolution at the 57th AGM. No amount is transferred from the Profit and Loss Account to reserves as provision for the proposed dividend. Balance sheet and reinvestment intent: the Company is engaged only in trading and its financial asset is mainly investment in listed security; there are no loans given and no guarantees issued by the Company, and details of investments fall under Section 186 of the Companies Act. Proceeds from the shareholder-approved inter-se transfer of UPL Limited shares to promoter-group entity Nerka Chemicals Private Limited were applied to subscription and to the first and second call money on UPL Limited's Rights Issue, leaving all shares allotted to the Company fully paid. No shares with differential voting rights, sweat equity shares or employee stock options were issued during the year, and there is no scheme for provision of money to buy the Company's own shares for employees or trustees. Related-party transactions are stated to be made on terms equivalent to arm's length, with year-end balances unsecured, interest free and settled in cash, and no guarantees given or received.
- No specific ESG commitments, goals or targets with defined timelines are set by the entity - BRSR Section B items 5 and 6 are reported as '-' for all nine NGRBC principles.
- No national or international codes, certifications, labels or standards (e.g. SA 8000, OHSAS, ISO, BIS) have been adopted and mapped to any principle - reported as 'No' for all nine principles.
- Sole material responsible business conduct issue identified is 'ESG and Regulatory Compliance', treated as a risk with negative financial implications, to be mitigated through improved business practices and governance with a focus on complete compliance.
- Highest authority responsible for implementation and oversight of the Business Responsibility policies is Mrs. Sandra Rajnikant Shroff, Managing Director (DIN: 00189012); there is no Board committee or director specified for decision-making on sustainability issues.
- Policies cover all nine NGRBC principles and have been translated into procedures, but only some policies have been approved by the Board as per relevant statutory requirements, and the policies are not applied to value chain partners.
- No independent external assessment or evaluation of the working of the policies has been carried out - the Company reviews the working of its policies internally, with Board review of performance against policies 'periodically / need based' and of statutory compliance on an ongoing basis.
- Grievance mechanisms: a Whistle Blower Policy is in place for communities, employees and customers, and a Stakeholders Relationship Committee redresses investor grievances with a report placed before the Board every quarter; shareholders have no separate written policy, the mechanism forming part of the corporate governance framework, and shareholder complaints are recorded as 'Resolved'.
- CSR under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 is not applicable to the Company; the BRSR is prepared on a standalone basis, is in its fourth year, reports essential indicators only, and has no assurance provider (assurance 'Not Applicable').
- Most BRSR reporting requirements are stated to be not applicable because the main objects are trading in chemicals and agro commodities and investment in securities and mutual funds, employees work for the Company on deputation and there are no workers.
- Diversity: women constitute 33.33% of the Board of Directors and 33.33% of Key Management Personnel as on 31st March, 2026; the BRSR states the business responsibility and sustainability strategy is guided by core values of excellence, integrity, respect and collaboration.

The only capital deployment described is financial rather than physical: under the shareholder approval taken at the 55th AGM, the Company inter-se transferred 9,80,000 equity shares of UPL Limited to promoter-group entity Nerka Chemicals Private Limited during the year (after 17,80,000 shares in FY2024-25) and used the consideration to pay the second call money, including premium of ` 180 per equity share, on the UPL Limited Rights Issue, so that all 49,49,947 equity shares allotted to the Company are now fully paid up. risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Investment concentration / capital-market volatility — The Company's financial asset is mainly investment in listed security, so any material volatility in the capital market may impact the market value of the investment. Income from investments (dividend on equity shares and mutual funds and interest on bank fixed deposits) is disclosed in the BRSR as a large share of turnover, and the year's step-up in other income and profit was attributed to a higher dividend declaration by UPL Limited of 300% versus 50% in the previous year - making earnings dependent on one investee's payout decision.
- Funding risk — As there are only trading activities in the Company, it may not be able to mobilize adequate funds, if any, in time. Management's stated mitigant is that the Company has good investment in quoted shares, so raising additional funds, if any, will not be difficult.
- Trading business / counterparty and contract-performance risk — Deals in agro commodities, metals and chemicals are done through sale and purchase contracts at pre-determined rates and quantities with the help of market intermediaries; there can be risks of unfulfillment of contractual terms - non-delivery, late or short delivery, quality issues on the supply side and non-payment from the customer side. The Company also transacts on the MCX Commodity platform through an intermediary registered with MCX/SEBI, doing deals only when spot and future rates differ.
- Single-activity / single-segment concentration — The Company is engaged only in trading and operates in a single segment; exports are reported as 'Not Applicable-0%' of turnover, employees work for the Company on deputation and it has no workers, so the business depends on group resources and on a narrow activity base with no diversification cushion.
- Regulatory risk — Any change in Government / Regulators Policy / Rules / Regulations will require fresh compliances; the stated mitigant is that the group has a very strong and dedicated team of professionals to study regulatory changes and fresh requirements.
- Foreign currency fluctuation risk — Trading activities may be subject to the risk of lower profit or loss on account of volatility in foreign currency exchange; management states it structures trading transactions so that such volatility risk is minimal, or may take adequate forward cover.
- Cyber security risk — The Company is subject to risks associated with IT and cybersecurity relating to cybercrime and theft of sensitive information; mitigants cited are group IT infrastructure and security systems with robust firewalls and disaster recovery mechanisms, perpetual event monitoring, access controls and employee education on safe practices.
- ESG and regulatory compliance (sole BRSR material issue) — The BRSR material responsible business conduct table identifies exactly one issue - 'ESG and Regulatory Compliance', flagged as a Risk with negative financial implications - linked to non-adherence with standards and guidelines of all regulatory agencies, to be mitigated by improved business practices and governance with a focus on complete compliance.
- External/environmental factors flagged in the cautionary statement — Management names drought or shortfall in rains, change in government policies, tariff barriers, delay in registrations, and changes in local and overseas markets as the factors that may affect performance - relevant to an agro-commodity trading book.
